title: Derive Macros Deep
concept: Derive macros auto-generate interface implementations from your type definition — `#[derive(Eq, Hash, Debug)]` writes the boilerplate for you.
why: Manually implementing Clone, Eq, Hash, Debug, and Display for every type is tedious and error-prone. Derive macros eliminate this boilerplate entirely.
tips: Use derive aggressively — it eliminates boilerplate and prevents copy-paste errors
Derive Debug for EVERY public type — future you will thank you during debugging
If a field doesn't implement the interface, implement it manually or skip that derive
Combine derives: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Eq, Hash)] is the standard 'data type' set
common_mistakes: Forgetting that all fields must implement the derived interface — compile error
Deriving Ord without deriving Eq — Ord requires Eq
Deriving Clone on types with heap data — be aware of the cost of deep copying
